beats.narration: OpenAI's open-weight model gives every attention head a way to look at nothing at all. Why does that matter, and what do the sliding windows save?
beats.narration_text: gpt-oss-120b: (1) explain the learned attention sink in each head, (2) show me the sliding-window vs full attention layout, (3) compute what that layout saves in KV cache at 131,072 tokens — from config.json.

props.title: gpt-oss, Paying Attention to Nothing?
thesis: 117B parameters, 5.1B active per token. One learned number per head lets
attention go nowhere — and half the layers only look 128 tokens back.

roadmap.label: The sink
roadmap.body: A learned logit per head, in the softmax denominator.

roadmap.label: The limits
roadmap.body: Open weights, closed recipe — measure the sink yourself.

props.source: OpenAI — gpt-oss-120b & gpt-oss-20b Model Card, arXiv:2508.10925 §2.2 · openai/gpt-oss-120b config.json

beats.narration: The thirty-six layers alternate. Half see only the last hundred twenty-eight tokens; half see the whole context. Each token also visits four of a hundred twenty-eight experts.
beats.narration_text: The thirty-six layers alternate. Half see only the last hundred twenty-eight tokens; half see the whole context. Each token also visits four of a hundred twenty-eight experts.

props.heading: Short window, full window

moves.label: SLIDING
moves.detail: Layers 1, 3, 5 … 35: each token sees the last 128.

moves.label: FULL
moves.detail: Layers 2, 4, 6 … 36: each token sees everything before it.

moves.label: EXPERTS
moves.detail: Mixture of experts: 4 of 128 experts per token.

props.keepNote: Only the 18 full layers grow with context — that is where the memory goes.
props.source: openai/gpt-oss-120b config.json · OpenAI — gpt-oss-120b & gpt-oss-20b Model Card, arXiv:2508.10925 §2.2

beats.narration: Normal attention must spend all its weight: the weights sum to one. gpt-oss adds one learned number per head to the softmax denominator. When nothing matters, the sink soaks up the weight.
beats.narration_text: Normal attention must spend all its weight: the weights sum to one. gpt-oss adds one learned number per head to the softmax denominator. When nothing matters, the sink soaks up the weight.

props.spark: A place to put attention you don't need.
props.heading: Softmax with a sink

moves.label: SOFTMAX
moves.detail: Ordinary attention: weights over real tokens always sum to 1.

moves.label: SINK
moves.detail: One learned logit per head joins the softmax denominator.

moves.label: EFFECT
moves.detail: Weights over real tokens can now sum to less than 1.

moves.label: OPT OUT
moves.detail: Nothing relevant? The sink takes the mass; the head attends to almost nothing.

props.keepNote: Per the model card, it lets a head pay no attention to any token.
props.source: OpenAI — gpt-oss-120b & gpt-oss-20b Model Card, arXiv:2508.10925 §2.2 — “a learned bias in the denominator of the softmax”

beats.narration: Now memory, at a hundred thirty-one thousand tokens. The eighteen full layers cache about four point eight gigabytes; the sliding layers barely register. All full would double it.
beats.narration_text: Now memory, at a hundred thirty-one thousand tokens. The eighteen full layers cache about four point eight gigabytes; the sliding layers barely register. All full would double it.

props.spark: Half the layers, half the cache.
props.heading: KV cache at 131,072 tokens
props.exception: Per full layer, per token: 8 KV heads × 64 dims × 2 (K, V) × 2 bytes = 2,048 bytes.
props.source: Computed from openai/gpt-oss-120b config.json (num_key_value_heads 8, head_dim 64, sliding_window 128) · BF16 cache assumed

beats.narration: Two limits. The weights are open; the training data isn't, so we see the design, not the recipe. And what each head learns to ignore isn't documented. You'd have to measure it yourself.
beats.narration_text: Two limits. The weights are open; the training data isn't, so we see the design, not the recipe. And what each head learns to ignore isn't documented. You'd have to measure it yourself.

props.heading: What the weights can't tell us

moves.label: DATA
moves.detail: Weights and model card are released; the training data is not.

moves.label: SINK
moves.detail: One learned scalar per head; what each head ignores isn't documented.

moves.label: MXFP4
moves.detail: MoE weights at 4.25 bits per parameter let 120b fit one 80 GB GPU.

props.keepNote: You can verify the layout from config.json. You cannot verify the recipe.
props.source: OpenAI — gpt-oss-120b & gpt-oss-20b Model Card, arXiv:2508.10925 §2.1, §2.2, §2.4 · config.json quantization_config

beats.narration: The verdict. The sink is a small change with a clear purpose: permission to do nothing. The alternating layout halves the cache. The training recipe stays closed.
beats.narration_text: The verdict. The sink is a small change with a clear purpose: permission to do nothing. The alternating layout halves the cache. The training recipe stays closed.

artifactLines: Sink: one learned logit per head lets attention over real tokens sum to less than one.
Memory: only full layers grow with context — ~4.8 GB at 131K vs ~9.7 GB all-full.
Limit: open weights, not open data; per-head sink behaviour is unmeasured here.
